1. Same medicine inside. Ozempic, Wegovy and Rybelsus all contain semaglutide, made by Novo Nordisk.
  2. Different jobs. Ozempic and Rybelsus are for type 2 diabetes. Wegovy is for weight management.
  3. Different forms. Ozempic and Wegovy are weekly injections; Rybelsus is a daily tablet. In 2026, the US also gained a Wegovy pill, and Rybelsus was renamed Ozempic tablets there.
  4. Not all are in Indonesia. Ozempic and Wegovy are registered with BPOM. We found no Indonesian registration for Rybelsus.

If you have heard all three names and wondered whether they are different drugs, you are not alone. They are one molecule sold in different forms, at different doses, for different conditions.

Below, we compare the three brands side by side, explain what each one is approved for, how the injections and tablets differ, and which ones you can get in Indonesia.

One Molecule: Semaglutide

All three brands contain the same active ingredient, semaglutide. If you want to understand what it does in the body, we explain how semaglutide works in a separate guide.

In short, semaglutide is a GLP-1 receptor agonist. It copies GLP-1, a hormone your gut releases after meals, which helps lower blood sugar and makes you feel full sooner. Novo Nordisk sells it under different brand names because each product is approved for a different condition, at a different dose, in a different form.

So choosing between Ozempic, Wegovy and Rybelsus comes down to your diagnosis, and whether a weekly injection or a daily tablet suits you better.

Ozempic vs Wegovy vs Rybelsus at a Glance

Here is how the semaglutide products compare on their US labels, plus their status in Indonesia.

Product Form How often Approved for (US) Highest dose on the US label Registered in Indonesia
Ozempic injection Injection pen Once a week Type 2 diabetes; also lowers heart and kidney risks in some adults with type 2 diabetes 2 mg Yes
Wegovy injection Injection pen Once a week Weight management; lowering heart risk in adults with heart disease; a type of fatty liver disease (MASH) 2.4 mg, or 7.2 mg as Wegovy HD Yes
Rybelsus (Ozempic tablets in the US since 2026) Tablet Once a day Type 2 diabetes 14 mg (Rybelsus) or 9 mg (Ozempic tablets) Not found
Wegovy pill Tablet Once a day Weight management 25 mg Not found

Two patterns stand out. The weight-management products use higher doses than the diabetes products, and the tablets need much higher milligram doses than the injections, because only a small share of a swallowed dose is absorbed.

How Is Each Semaglutide Brand Different?

Each brand has its own approved uses, doses and history. Here is what sets them apart.

Ozempic: Weekly Injection for Type 2 Diabetes

Ozempic was approved in the US in December 2017 to help adults with type 2 diabetes control their blood sugar, alongside diet and exercise. Its label has since grown to include lowering the risk of heart attack and stroke in adults with type 2 diabetes and heart disease, and slowing kidney decline in those with chronic kidney disease. Many people lose weight on Ozempic, but weight loss is not one of its approved uses.

Wegovy: Weekly Injection, and Now a Pill, for Weight Management

Wegovy was approved in June 2021 for long-term weight management, at a higher weekly dose than Ozempic. In the US, two new options followed. The Wegovy pill, a 25 mg daily tablet, was approved in December 2025; in its main trial, people lost an average of 13.6% of their body weight over 64 weeks, compared with 2.2% on placebo. Wegovy HD, a 7.2 mg weekly injection, followed in March 2026 for adults who have tolerated the 2.4 mg dose for at least four weeks.

Rybelsus: Daily Tablet for Type 2 Diabetes

Rybelsus became the first GLP-1 tablet when it was approved in September 2019, for adults with type 2 diabetes. In early 2026, the US approved a new formulation under the name Ozempic tablets, in 1.5, 4 and 9 mg strengths. The label notes that these new tablets and the older Rybelsus 3, 7 and 14 mg tablets are not interchangeable milligram for milligram. Outside the US, the Rybelsus name may still be in use.

Injection or Tablet: How Do the Formats Compare?

The biggest practical difference between the brands is how you take them. One is a weekly routine, the other a daily one.

Weekly Injections: Ozempic and Wegovy

Ozempic comes in a multi-use pen, sold as the FlexTouch pen in many countries, that delivers several weekly doses. Wegovy comes in pens that are either single-dose (in the US) or multi-use FlexTouch pens (in markets such as the UK). Either way, you inject once a week, on the same day each week, under the skin of your stomach, thigh or upper arm. Pens are personal and should never be shared, even with a new needle.

Daily Tablets: Rybelsus and the Wegovy Pill

Tablets avoid needles but come with strict rules, because food and drink reduce how much semaglutide is absorbed. The Rybelsus and Ozempic tablet label says to take the tablet in the morning on an empty stomach, with no more than 4 ounces (about 120 ml) of plain water. You then wait at least 30 minutes before eating, drinking or taking other tablets.

Which Format Suits You?

If you are comfortable with a small weekly injection, a pen means one dose a week and no daily routine. If you prefer to avoid needles and can keep a strict morning routine, a tablet may suit you better. Your doctor will weigh this alongside your diagnosis and the products available where you live.

Which Semaglutide Brands Are Registered in Indonesia?

In Indonesia, two semaglutide brands are registered with BPOM, and both are prescription medicines:

  • Ozempic, for type 2 diabetes, registration number DKI2164605043A1 (record)
  • Wegovy, for weight management, registration numbers DKI2464605443A1 and DKI2464605443B1 (record)

We found no Indonesian registration for Rybelsus, the Wegovy pill or the new Ozempic tablets. In practice, that means the semaglutide options a doctor in Indonesia can prescribe are the two weekly injections. You can check any pack’s number on BPOM’s official checker, cekbpom.pom.go.id.

Can You Switch Between Ozempic, Wegovy and Rybelsus?

Yes, but only with your doctor’s guidance. Because they contain the same molecule, switching is common, for example when someone moves from a diabetes product to a weight-management one, or from a tablet to an injection.

A few points matter when you switch:

  • Doses do not convert one to one. A tablet dose in milligrams is not the same as an injection dose, and even the old and new semaglutide tablets are not interchangeable milligram for milligram. Your doctor will choose the starting dose.
  • Never use two semaglutide products at once. Taking Ozempic and Wegovy together, for example, doubles up on the same drug.
  • Expect some stomach side effects again. Moving to a higher dose can bring back nausea for a while, as it did when you first started.
  • Learn the new device or routine. A new pen or a tablet with fasting rules works differently from what you are used to.

Conclusion

Ozempic, Wegovy and Rybelsus are three ways of taking the same medicine, semaglutide. Ozempic is a weekly injection for type 2 diabetes, Wegovy is a weekly injection for weight management at a higher dose, and Rybelsus is a daily tablet for type 2 diabetes. In the US, the line-up has grown with the Wegovy pill and Wegovy HD, and Rybelsus has been renamed Ozempic tablets.

In Indonesia, the registered options are Ozempic and Wegovy, both on prescription. The right product depends on your diagnosis and whether you prefer a weekly injection or a daily tablet, so talk to your doctor before starting or switching.

Frequently Asked Questions

Is Ozempic the Same as Wegovy?

Yes, in what they contain: both are semaglutide injections from Novo Nordisk. They differ in approved use and dose. Ozempic is for type 2 diabetes, and Wegovy is for weight management at a higher dose.

Can Ozempic Be Used for Weight Loss?

Weight loss is not one of Ozempic’s approved uses, although many people lose weight on it. The semaglutide brand approved for weight management is Wegovy.

Which Is Stronger, Ozempic or Wegovy?

Wegovy goes up to a higher weekly dose: 2.4 mg, or 7.2 mg as Wegovy HD in the US, compared with 2 mg for Ozempic. The molecule is the same.

What Is the Ozempic Pill?

It is the US name, since 2026, for Novo Nordisk’s new semaglutide tablets, which replace Rybelsus there. Like Rybelsus, they are for type 2 diabetes.

Is Rybelsus Available in Indonesia?

We found no BPOM registration for Rybelsus. In Indonesia, the registered semaglutide brands are Ozempic and Wegovy, both weekly injections.

Does Rybelsus Have to Be Taken on an Empty Stomach?

Yes. Take it in the morning with a small amount of plain water, then wait at least 30 minutes before eating, drinking or taking other tablets.

Do Ozempic, Wegovy and Rybelsus Have the Same Side Effects?

Yes, the types are the same, mainly nausea, diarrhoea, vomiting and constipation. They tend to be more frequent at the higher doses used for weight management.
